summary: Per-frame vehicle update that consumes fuel, recomputes total mass, applies tire wear and tire friction, re-seeds weather-driven grip noise about every 5.5 seconds, and drives a per-wheel random failure engine (engine/gearbox/puncture/random wear) gated on the race being in progress. Called every frame from MainGameTickUpdate.

operations.description: If fuel level (this[3678]) is positive, decrement fuel by engine RPM (this[3685]) * engine power factor (this[3681]) * throttle (this[3420]) * dt (a2).
When fuel drops to or below 0, clamp fuel to 0 and, through the object pointer at this[0], write error code 9 to the error register (obj+0x4068) if it is not already set (out of fuel).
Recompute total mass (this[3397]) = fuel * 0.75 + base mass (this[3396]) and inverse total mass (this[3398]) = 1.0 / total mass.
Sum the per-tire wear accumulators over 4 wheels (this[3444], stride 62) into a single wear total.
Grip decay factor = 1.0 - wearTotal * 0.2325.

For each of 4 wheels: if the per-wheel wear source is positive, decrement tire wear level (this[3468]) by gripFactor * wearSource * wear-rate factor (this[3469]) * tireWearMultiplier (dword_7D0C60) * dt, then clamp the wear level at a minimum of 0.75.

Per wheel: tire friction (this[3464]) = previous + (next - previous) * track grip (flt_8AFEE8), then scaled by tire wear level (this[3468]) * friction multiplier (this[3837]) * grip interpolation (flt_8ACED0 + (flt_8ACED4 - flt_8ACED0) * flt_8AFEE8).

If |session time (dbl_8AFEA0) - last weather-noise update (this[3838])| > 5.5, reseed last weather-noise update from the weather noise table (flt_8AB274[dword_8AAE70++]) and recompute tire brush forces via TireBrushModelForceSolver.
Failure event processing runs only when sub_4D21D0() returns true (race in progress).
For wheels i = 0..3: if the failure countdown (this[3929+i]) is >= 0, decrement it by dt; when it drops below 0, dispatch the failure type by wheel index through the switch jump table (jpt_4EDBA3).
Engine failure (case 0): write error code 1 to the error register (obj+0x4068) if not already set.
If engine RPM (this[3685]) is below 50% of the RPM limit (this[3686]), suppress the failure by resetting the countdown to 0.

Engine failure branch: if any engine power factor (this[3922]/this[3923]/this[3924]) is nonzero, or the noise draw (flt_8AAE74[dword_8AAE70++]) is >= 0.5, regenerate the power factors from the noise table; otherwise decay the engine power table entries and select one factor to regenerate.
Reset engine power table: for j < this[3692] entries, set the paired value (offset +4 of each 8-byte entry) of the table pointed to by this[3689] to 0.

Decay alternative: multiply each engine power table entry by 0.9, mark one engine power factor with the -789.0 sentinel, compute a new failure countdown from the noise draw (bands x1000 / x450 / x50), and if wear mode (dword_7CEA5C) == 3 cap the countdown at 60.
Complete engine failure: set failure mode state (this[3928]) = 2 and post the event via sub_41AC50(object, 0).
Gearbox failure (case 1): write error code 5 to the error register (obj+0x4068) if not already set.
If gearbox health threshold (this[3422]) is 0, skip the gearbox failure (countdown reset to 0).
On gearbox failure, scale one of the two gearbox wear factors (this[3724] or this[3729], chosen by noise draw from flt_8AB274[dword_8AAE70++]) by 0.03125.
Complete gearbox failure: set failure mode state (this[3928]) = 2 and post the event via sub_41AC50(object, 1).
Puncture failure (case 2): write error code 2 to the error register (obj+0x4068) if not already set.
Puncture: set the puncture flag byte (this+0x39EE) to 1 and, when failure mode state (this[3928]) == 0, set it to 1.
Post the puncture event via sub_41AC50(object, 2).
Random wear failure (case 3): write error code 4 to the error register (obj+0x4068) if not already set.
Random wear: choose a wheel via RandLCGRandomNumberGenerator(...) % 4 and add 0.05 to that wheel's wear accumulator (this[3448 + 62*wheel]).
Random wear skip: if the comparison flags from the preceding checks indicate a skip condition, reset the countdown to 0 instead of triggering random wear.
Complete random-wear failure: set failure mode state (this[3928]) = 2 and post the event via sub_41AC50(object, 3).

this->tireFriction[w] = lerp(this->tireFriction[w], this->tireFriction[w + 1], TrackGrip) * this->tireWearLevel[w] * this->frictionMultiplier * gripInterp;
